\caption{\textbf{Independent Source-Model KGA Routing Evaluation and Published Baseline Comparison (Tasks 1 \& 3).} Evaluation across three independently trained ResNet-18 source checkpoints ($N=36$ cells per model; Model 0 canonical seed 0, Model 101 independent seed 101, Model 102 independent seed 102). \textbf{Panel A} reports within-model replication on the original uniformly helpful 36-condition panel ($\Delta > 0$). \textbf{Panel B} reports the balanced mixed-sign replication panel deliberately containing 39--42\% negative-benefit conditions ($\Delta < 0$); separately, 11--14\% of conditions had absolute measured benefit within 1 percentage point of zero ($|\Delta| \le 0.01$). Under leave-one-out (LOO) empirical residual calibration (within-model leave-one-condition-out calibration on the evaluated checkpoint, which pools peer cells from the evaluated model), KGA achieved lower point oracle regret than both Always Freeze ($R_{\mathrm{AF}} = 12.67$--$14.12\%$) and Always Adapt ($R_{\mathrm{AA}} = 1.01$--$1.39\%$) on each checkpoint ($R_{\mathrm{policy}} = 0.08$--$0.23\%$, $\mathrm{FA}_u \le 0.0278$). \textbf{Panel C} compares KGA against the published AETTA baseline (Lee et al., CVPR 2024; native MC-dropout accuracy estimator and recovery decision rule) under both within-model LOO and 3-way outcome-disjoint cross-fitting (B6). Under LOO, KGA achieves lower point oracle regret than AETTA ($0.08$--$0.23\%$ vs $0.18$--$0.36\%$, a regret gap of $+0.09$ to $+0.28\text{ pp}$). Under outcome-disjoint cross-fitting (B6), KGA achieves lower regret than both fixed policies on every model ($R_{\mathrm{KGA}} < R_{\mathrm{AA}} < R_{\mathrm{AF}}$), but exhibits an empirical tradeoff with AETTA: B6 incurs higher point regret ($0.23$--$1.14\%$ vs $0.18$--$0.36\%$, a regret gap of $-0.05$ to $-0.78\text{ pp}$ relative to AETTA) while committing zero observed false adaptations ($\mathrm{FA}_u = 0.0000$ across all models, vs $4$--$5$ observed false adaptations committed by AETTA, $\mathrm{FA}_u = 0.1111$--$0.1389$).}
